A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we present a new parallel divide and conquer algorithm which uses two dimensional block cyclic distributions and the Lowner approach to compute orthogonal matrices and that we introduce permutations before each rank-one update to make good use of the cache.

the implementation we present is the fastest implementation of the divide and conquer algorithm to date on distributed memory architectures, that it scales well on a large number of processors and that it can solve very large problems.

we present a new parallel divide and conquer implementation of the tridiagonal eigenvalue problem which has the best known performance on distributed memory architectures and is competitive with other parallel implementations on shared memory architectures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a two dimensional block distribution is a viable alternative to the one dimensional block distribution that has been used in the past.
the two dimensional block cyclic approach is more e cient than the one dimensional approach, even when the latter is used in conjunction with the Lowner algorithm for computing the eigenvectors.
